text:
sasha: Heads-up — we had a customer hit 100% saturation on their primary model pool and our fallback kicked in but cost jumped 3x. Need to discuss smarter capacity-based failover behavior.

alex: ugh. can you paste the console trace? which fallback variant did we pick?

sasha: pasted below from console logs: 
```
[2026-03-12T16:34:21Z] route=prod-eu customer=big-retailer model=redwood-7b v1 pool_saturation=1.00 -> selected variant redwood-7b-quantized-1 (region=fallback-us)
[2026-03-12T16:34:21Z] note: variant latency ok but cost_mult=3.2
```

mira: was PreferRegionalFallback enabled for that tenant? if not we probably routed cross-region which explains cost bump (+egress) and higher latency.

sasha: tenant had tier=pro, PreferRegionalFallback=false (they opted for lowest-p-cost).

jordan: two quick proposals: (A) add a capacity-aware cost penalty in routing score so we prefer slightly-more-expensive-but-local variant over cheap-distant one when saturation is high, or (B) add a per-tenant cost cap that prevents cross-region fallback if predicted unit cost > X.

emily: from PM side — we need predictable SLOs for pro tier. If we silently pick a variant that triples cost we break their budget alerts. We should surface when fallback will materially change unit cost.

alex: +1 on surfacing. also suggest an option in Console rollout UX: "Auto-fallback aggressiveness" with three presets: conservative / normal / aggressive. conservative = prefer regional & cost-aware, aggressive = prioritize lowest latency/cost regardless of region.

sasha: mockup idea for console text: "Auto-fallback aggressiveness — controls willingness to cross-region or deviate to heavier quantized variants when pools are saturated. Includes estimated delta on per-token cost."

mira: telemetry side — we need better signals before and after fallback: routing.fallback.count, model.saturation_pct, fallback.cost_multiplier_predicted, fallback.cost_multiplier_observed. Also link the tenant alert if observed > predicted by 20%.

jordan: implementation note: routing currently uses score = weight_latency * est_latency + weight_cost * est_cost + penalty_if_saturated. Proposed change: compute cost_with_egress and add dynamic_penalty = alpha * max(0, saturation - S_thresh) * cost_with_egress. Pseudocode: 
```
score(variant) = latency_score + cost_score + dynamic_penalty
where dynamic_penalty = alpha * max(0, pool_saturation - 0.75) * cost_with_egress
```

sasha: that would bias away from fully-saturated pools unless tenant explicitly allows cross-region. good. we also need a per-tenant override API: POST /routing/tenants/{id}/fallback-config {"aggressiveness":"conservative"}.

alex: can we make the default conservative for enterprise/prod tenants and normal for free/trial? reduces billing surprises.

emily: yes, and add a rollout flag so we can flip for a subset of customers via canary. product wants a staged rollout with telemetry gates.

deploy-bot: deploy plan created — feature/auto-fallback-penalty -> staging (canary 5%) -> production. CI: 14 tests, 0 failures.

mira: one more ask — expose in Console per-route preview: "If auto-fallback applied, estimated cost delta: +X% and expected latency change: +Yms". Should be based on historical variant cost and kv_cache_hit_rate adjustments.

sasha: agreed. I'll draft an RFC with sample config, metrics names, and console mockups. tagging @alex @mira for review. :rocket:

alex: thanks — pls include a short fallback decision log line for each request so we can debug shards where the weighting flip happened. minimal fields: request_id, tenant_id, primary_pool_saturation, chosen_variant, predicted_cost_mult, reason_code.

sasha: noted. will include.

emily: pm note — also capture customer-visible notification wording for budget alerts when observed cost exceeds expected by >25%.

jordan: ok i'm going to prototype the dynamic_penalty branch this afternoon. will post perf numbers.

sasha: perfect. wrapping up — RFC target EOD Fri. we want canary next week.
